analysis: This PR is documentation-only. It adds docs/operations/desktop-release.md, links it from docs/operations/README.md (line 10), and adds a pointer in docs/developer/desktop-app.md (head lines 537-539) to the .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml release process. No source code, workflow file, or threat-model control is changed in the supplied units. The workflow file is referenced but not supplied, so its actual behavior (secret handling, tag trigger permissions, signing verification, CLI prerequisite check) is unverified. The docs claim the workflow reuses the provider-release Developer ID (team SLDQ2GJ6TL) and notarization secrets, verifies tag/version match, notarization, stapling, bundle ID and the installer script, and refuses publication if the latest CLI lacks DesktopCommand.swift. These claims affect artifact integrity (T-013/T-034 area, A-011 only indirectly) and desktop distribution, which is outside the provider threat model's core scope. Points for the next pass if the workflow is in scope: pin third-party actions, restrict tag-push authorization (tag protection), keep the signing keychain scoped to release jobs, and ensure dry-run workflow_dispatch runs don't expose secrets to untrusted branches. The docs state that auto-update is not configured and that the GUI never uses provider releases as a feed, consistent with existing desktop-app.md guidance. The docs also state that qualification on real hardware remains required and don't claim attestation qualification. No regression is identified from the doc text itself.
